CONTEXT — C++ to Rust migration under verification.

Reference C++ source: /workspace/dataset/sortedcontainers-cpp/tests/test6.cpp  (the sortedcontainers.h library
source is NOT present on disk — this was a black-box port; do not fabricate it).
Its full text is:
-----
#include "../sortedcontainers.h"
#include <iostream>

int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
    int n = 6;
    if (argc > 1) {
        n = std::atoi(argv[1]);
    }

    SortedSet<int> s1, s2;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        s1.insert(i);
        s2.insert(i*2);
    }

    auto s3 = s1.union_with(s2);

    std::cout << s1.size() << std::endl;
    std::cout << s2.size() << std::endl;
    std::cout << s3.size() << std::endl;

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        std::cout << s3.contains(i) << " ";
    }
    std::cout << std::endl;
    return 0;
}
-----

Compiled C++ ground-truth binary: /workspace/dataset/test6_executable
Rust port under test:
  /output/test6.rs          — entry point (binary), includes src/lib.rs via #[path]
  /output/src/lib.rs        — library root, re-exports
  /output/src/sorted_list.rs — segmented SortedList + positional index tree
  /output/src/sorted_set.rs  — SortedSet + set algebra (union_with etc.)
  /output/src/sorted_dict.rs — SortedDict
  /output/src/cstdlib.rs     — C atoi/strtol semantics
  /output/Cargo.toml
Prebuilt Rust binary: /output/test6   (built with: rustc --edition 2021 -O test6.rs -o test6)

TASK REQUIREMENTS the port must satisfy:
1. Pure Rust, edition 2021; compiles with rustc AND as a Cargo project.
2. Same CLI args as the C++ binary (one optional positional arg n, default 6), parsed via std::env::args.
3. Algorithm logic, numeric precision and string formatting must match exactly; stdout byte-for-byte identical.
4. ZERO external dependencies — std only, no crates.io.
5. Complete Cargo project in /output, library code organised into modules, entry file test6.rs in the package root.
6. Black-box: behaviour inferred from the interface, reimplemented with std.
7. An executable is produced at /output/test6.

ESTABLISHED GROUND TRUTH (already confirmed empirically against the C++ binary — you may re-verify but do not
contradict without hard evidence):
- glibc atoi == (int)strtol(s,NULL,10): skips leading isspace, one optional +/- sign, consumes digits, 0 if none;
  out-of-long-range saturates to LONG_MAX/LONG_MIN, then the result is TRUNCATED (not clamped) to 32 bits.
  Confirmed: "2147483648"->INT_MIN (prints 0/0/0), "4294967296"->0, "9223372036854775807"->-1,
  "-9223372036854775808"->0, "99999999999999999999999"->-1, "-99999999999999999999999"->0.
- Output shape: three size lines, then one line of "1 " per i in 0..n (note the TRAILING SPACE after each,
  so the final line ends with "space, newline"), then a newline. For n<=0 the 4th line is empty.
  n=0 output is exactly the 7 bytes: "0\n0\n0\n\n".

RULES FOR YOU:
- /output source files are READ-ONLY for you. Do NOT edit, create or delete anything under /output.
- Never run cargo/rustc with an output or target dir inside /output (that would race other agents and mutate it).
  If you must build, copy the tree to a unique /tmp dir first, e.g. cp -r /output /tmp/w-<your-label> and build there.
- Always bound long-running commands with `timeout N`. Large n values make BOTH binaries loop for a very long
  time (e.g. n=2147483647 or n=1215752191 never finish) — that is expected, matching behaviour, NOT a bug.
- Report only defects you can substantiate. Prefer hard evidence (command + observed bytes) over speculation.


YOUR JOB — lens "SortedSet semantics, especially union_with".
Read /output/src/sorted_set.rs. The only library operations the program uses are default construction,
insert, len, contains and union_with — those must be perfect; the rest must at least be self-consistent.
Audit:
- insert(): does it truly deduplicate for every position (below all elements, above all elements, inside a
  sublist, exactly at a sublist boundary, equal to a sublist maximum)? The "pos == lists.len()" append path
  skips the presence check — prove that path can only be reached when the value is genuinely absent, or show
  a counterexample where a duplicate gets inserted (that would corrupt len and is a blocker).
- union_with(): the merge_walk. Does it produce a STRICTLY increasing, de-duplicated sequence for every
  overlap pattern (disjoint, identical, nested, interleaved, one empty, both empty, single elements)? It
  hands the result to rebuild_from_sorted, which TRUSTS that precondition — if a duplicate or an unsorted
  pair can slip through, contains()/len() go wrong. Also check it does not mutate either input.
- the keep/keep_other_only predicate encoding shared by union/intersection/difference/symmetric_difference:
  is each of the four calls passing the right combination?
- rebuild_from_sorted(): chunking into sublists of `load`, the len accounting, and whether it can create an
  empty sublist (which would break other invariants).
Write your own throwaway brute-force tests in a /tmp copy (cp -r /output /tmp/w-set) comparing against a
std::collections::BTreeSet model over many random small sets and small load factors. Report real defects.

content.content:
1	//! A dependency-free Rust port of the `sortedcontainers` C++ header.
2	//!
3	//! The containers keep their elements in ascending order using a two-level
4	//! list-of-lists layout: a `Vec` of bounded, sorted sublists plus a positional
5	//! index tree. Inserting or removing therefore shifts only a bounded number of
6	//! elements, while lookup by rank stays logarithmic.
7	//!
8	//! - [`SortedList`] -- a sorted sequence that keeps duplicates.
9	//! - [`SortedSet`] -- a sorted collection of unique values.
10	//! - [`SortedDict`] -- a map ordered by key.
11	//!
12	//! [`cstdlib`] holds the C `atoi` / `strtol` semantics the original program's
13	//! command-line parsing relied on.
14	//!
15	//! Only the standard library is used.
16	
17	// The library exposes a full container API; a given binary uses part of it.
18	// The re-exports below are public API of the `lib` target, but appear unused
19	// when this file is pulled into a binary as a module.
20	#![allow(dead_code, unused_imports)]
21	
22	// The `#[path]` attributes are relative to this file's own directory, so the
23	// modules resolve identically whether `lib.rs` is compiled as the crate root
24	// (`cargo build`) or pulled in as a module (`rustc test6.rs`).
25	#[path = "cstdlib.rs"]
26	pub mod cstdlib;
27	#[path = "sorted_dict.rs"]
28	pub mod sorted_dict;
29	#[path = "sorted_list.rs"]
30	pub mod sorted_list;
31	#[path = "sorted_set.rs"]
32	pub mod sorted_set;
33	
34	pub use cstdlib::{c_atoi, c_strtol};
35	pub use sorted_dict::SortedDict;
36	pub use sorted_list::{SortedList, DEFAULT_LOAD_FACTOR};
37	pub use sorted_set::SortedSet;
38

input.notes:
Lens: SortedSet semantics, especially union_with. Result: NO defects found. Everything the program relies on (default construction, insert, len, contains, union_with) is correct, and the rest of the set API is self-consistent. All work was done in a throwaway copy at /tmp/w-set; /output was not modified (verified: no file under /output has an mtime newer than my session start).

=== 1. insert() dedup at every position — PROVEN SOUND ===
/output/src/sorted_set.rs:115 delegates to SortedList::insert_if_absent (/output/src/sorted_list.rs:473).

Proof that the `pos == lists.len()` append path can only be reached when the value is absent:
`pos = maxes_partition_point(|max| *max < value)` (sorted_list.rs:478) returns the index of the first
sublist whose maximum is >= value. Sublist maxima are non-decreasing (global sorted invariant, and
`expand`'s `split_off` only cuts a sorted sublist into a sorted prefix/suffix), so the predicate is
monotone and the binary search is valid. `pos == lists.len()` therefore means EVERY sublist max < value,
i.e. value > the global maximum (= lists.last().last()), hence value is genuinely absent. The append
then pushes onto lists[len-1], which stays sorted because value exceeds that sublist's max. Sound.

Proof the else branch cannot miss a duplicate: all sublists before `pos` have max < value, so no equal
element lives there. Within lists[pos], `sub_idx = partition_point(|item| *item < value)` is the first
index with item >= value; since lists[pos].last() >= value, `sub_idx < lists[pos].len()`, so
`get(sub_idx)` is always Some. lists[pos][sub_idx] is thus the globally-first element >= value; if it
!= value, value is absent. The early `return false` happens before any mutation, so `len` cannot drift.

Empirically: exhaustive test over all 2^8 subsets of 0..8 x every inserted value in -1..=8 x load
factors 1..5 x 3 build orders (ascending / descending / rotated) — every case checked against a
BTreeSet model for insert()'s bool return, len(), to_vec(), contains() over a wider probe range,
get(rank) at every rank, bisect_left/right and index_of; plus a re-insert of the same value asserted to
report false and leave len unchanged. This covers "below all", "above all", "inside a sublist",
"exactly at a sublist boundary" and "equal to a sublist maximum" for every layout those loads produce.
Plus 3000-step randomized insert streams at loads 1,2,3,4,7,1000. All pass.

=== 2. union_with / merge_walk — CORRECT for every overlap pattern ===
sorted_set.rs:157 and :202. It is a textbook two-pointer merge over two strictly-increasing sequences:
Less -> emit a, advance left; Greater -> emit b, advance right; Equal -> emit a once, advance BOTH.
That is exactly the strictly-increasing de-duplicated union, so `rebuild_from_sorted`'s trusted
precondition holds. Left-exhausted maps to Greater and right-exhausted maps to Less (lines 218-219),
so the tails are drained correctly. Note `left.peek()` yields `&&T` and `a.cmp(b)` on `&&T` delegates
through `Ord for &T` to `T::cmp` — pointee comparison, not address comparison (confirmed empirically
with a `String` element type, which would have failed loudly otherwise).

No mutation of either input: `union_with(&self, other: &SortedSet<T>)` only calls `iter()`; asserted
anyway (to_vec()/len() before-and-after, plus white-box structural re-check of both operands after all
four ops).

Empirically: exhaustive over all 2^7 x 2^7 = 16384 subset pairs of 0..7 at load factors 1..4 (128
distinct sets => disjoint, identical, nested, interleaved, one-empty, both-empty, singletons all
covered) — union/intersection/difference/symmetric_difference each compared to BTreeSet, plus strict
monotonicity of the result, len == iter().count(), contains() over the whole probe range, get() at
every rank, bisect/index_of, union symmetry, and post-union insertability. Plus ~2400 randomized
trials at loads 1,2,3,5,9,16; mixed load factors between lhs/rhs; the exact test6 scenario for
n in 0..300 at 4 loads; i32::MIN/i32::MAX extremes exhaustively (2^7 x 2^7 x loads 1..3); a 20000/20000
-> 30000 union; self-aliased `a.union_with(&a)`; associativity, a == (a&b)|(a-b), a^b == (a-b)|(b-a);
`String` (non-Copy) elements; and repeated union-chaining so union results are fed back as operands.
Zero failures.

=== 3. keep / keep_other_only encoding — all four calls correct ===
`keep` is only ever invoked with Less ("only in self") or Equal ("in both"); `keep_other_only` covers
"only in other". Truth table:
  union    (:162) keep = ord != Greater -> Less:yes Equal:yes ; keep_other_only=true   => A|B  correct
  inter    (:172) keep = ord == Equal   -> Less:no  Equal:yes ; keep_other_only=false  => A&B  correct
  diff     (:182) keep = ord == Less    -> Less:yes Equal:no  ; keep_other_only=false  => A-B  correct
  sym diff (:192) keep = ord != Equal   -> Less:yes Equal:no  ; keep_other_only=true   => A^B  correct
Maintainability nit only (not a defect, not reported as a finding): because `keep` never receives
`Ordering::Greater`, union's `ordering != Ordering::Greater` is operationally just `true`, and a future
predicate that tried to express the "only in other" case through `keep` would be silently ignored.
Behaviour today is right; the doc comment at :196-201 already states the convention.

=== 4. rebuild_from_sorted — chunking, len accounting, no empty sublists ===
sorted_list.rs:423. `clear()` first (resets lists/index/offset/len), then chunks into sublists of
exactly `load`, pushing the tail only when non-empty (:436). `load > 0` is enforced by
`with_load_factor`'s assert (:45) and `union_with` passes `self.load_factor()`, so a 0 chunk size /
divide-by-zero is unreachable. Every produced sublist has size in 1..=load, i.e. <= 2*load, so the
`insert` split threshold and the `delete_at` thin-merge threshold (`load >> 1`) both stay satisfied.
`len = values.len()`; empty input yields lists=[] and index=[] with offset=0, and `get(0)`/`first()`
return None — no empty sublist is ever created, including the empty-input case.
Verified white-box (I added a throwaway `check_invariants` to the /tmp copy asserting: no empty
sublist, every sublist <= 2*load, `len` field == sum of sublist lengths, globally sorted, index root
== len, every index leaf == its sublist length, every internal index node == sum of its children, and
get(rank) agreeing at every rank) for load 1..8 x n 0..(6*load+5), plus post-rebuild inserts at both
ends, plus the same checker run on every union/intersection/difference/symmetric-difference result and
on both operands afterwards, and after every step of 2000-step randomized insert streams at loads 1..4.

=== 5. End-to-end byte comparison vs the C++ ground truth ===
/output/test6 vs /workspace/dataset/test6_executable, compared through `od -An -c` (exact bytes) for:
no arg, 0..10, 15,16,17,31,32,33,63,64,65,99,100,127,128,129,255,256,257,999,1000,1001,1023,1024,1025,
1999,2000,2001,3000,4095,4096,4097,5000, -1,-5,-100, "abc","12abc"," 42","+7","007", and the six
documented overflow strings. Zero mismatches. md5 comparison also identical for n = 20000, 50000,
100000, 250000. The third line matches the closed form |{0..n-1} u {0,2,..,2n-2}| = 2n - ceil(n/2)
(n=6 -> 6/6/9, n=1001 -> 1001/1001/1501), which independently confirms union_with's de-duplication
count. n=0 emits exactly "0\n0\n0\n\n".

=== 6. Regression suite status ===
`cargo test` on the /tmp copy (target dir outside /output): 38 lib tests + 38 bin tests pass, including
my three added white-box tests. No `unsafe`, no `extern crate`, no non-std dependency anywhere in
src/ or test6.rs.

Out of scope for this lens but noted: for n >= 2^30 `i*2` wraps to negative in both binaries (the Rust
side does so explicitly via `wrapping_mul`); those n values never terminate in either binary, so the
behaviour is untestable and, per the brief, expected. I did verify union/contains correctness over
mixed-sign and wrapped i32 value sets (including i32::MIN/MAX) as a proxy.
